title: Prematurity — Classification & Complications by System
sources: Critical Vector — Neonatology Pocket Guide: Low Birth Weight & Prematurity

changelog.change: Initial entry — weight and gestational-age classification, GA assessment, the problems-by-organ-system table, and discharge-readiness criteria.

purpose: Classify by weight AND gestational age (they answer different questions), then run the organ-system checklist of prematurity complications and the discharge-readiness criteria.

rows: ≥ 4000 g, or > 90th percentile for gestational age
37 to < 42 weeks (early term 37–38+6, full term 39–40+6, late term 41+)

body.text: GA assessment: best is a first-trimester ultrasound; postnatally the New Ballard Score (6 physical + 6 neuromuscular maturity signs). LBW may be prematurity, growth restriction, or both — weight alone does not give the cause.

rows: RDS (surfactant deficiency), apnoea of prematurity, bronchopulmonary dysplasia
Intraventricular haemorrhage, HIE, sepsis/meningitis; long-term cerebral palsy, hydrocephalus
Hypotension, patent ductus arteriosus, early heart failure
Anaemia of prematurity, bleeding tendency, DIC
Necrotising enterocolitis, feeding intolerance, exaggerated jaundice
Poor water and solute handling; hypothermia (high surface-area-to-volume ratio, minimal subcutaneous fat)
Relative immunodeficiency → infection risk; retinopathy of prematurity (screen and treat — can cause blindness)

items: Consistent weight gain over several days.
Full oral feeding, tolerating volumes (suck–swallow–breathe coordination is usually adequate ≥ 34 weeks postmenstrual age; NG/OG feeds until then).
Stable temperature in an open cot.
No apnoea/bradycardia events for a defined observation window (commonly 5–7 days).
Newborn hearing screen done; retinopathy-of-prematurity eye exam completed / follow-up arranged; car-seat tolerance test if indicated.

buildNote: System-by-system checklist for the preterm infant; links to the specific neonatology modules for management.
